checked.comment: Matches Section 3. Rewards in [0,1], linear realizability with ||x||<=1 and ||theta*||<=1, K feature vectors per round chosen by an oblivious adversary, bandit feedback. SupLinUCB takes T as input and BaseLinUCB uses alpha, which depends on T, K and delta, so learner_knows is consistent.
Same problem class as s1, used by Theorem 2. Letting the learner know T, K and d is consistent with a fixed construction.

Theorem 1: with probability at least 1-delta, regret is O(sqrt(T d ln^3(KT ln T/delta))). The expression, high-probability type, known horizon (T is an input to SupLinUCB), tuning of alpha and the realized-reward per-round comparator are all correct.

Theorem 2: E[sum_t max_a x^T theta* - sum_t r_{t,a_t}] >= gamma sqrt(Td) for T>=K>=2 and d^2<=T. Max mean minus realized reward, in expectation, is pseudo-regret. Recording it as Omega(sqrt(Td)) for all algorithms is correct.

summary: The extraction is accurate. Theorem 1 (the high-probability upper bound for SupLinUCB) and Theorem 2 (the Omega(sqrt(Td)) lower bound) are recorded with the right expressions, conditions and qualifiers. The remaining lemmas are technical or restate prior work, and Lemma 7 is correctly placed in cited_results.
